messages.subject: grouping behavior in dplyr
messages.body_plain:
I'm seeing odd behavior applying dplyr verbs - arrange, for one - to a grouped data_frame.  At first, I thought it was related to a variable transformed by lubridate, but maybe it's something fundamental about grouping that I fail to grasp:

eg, given
library(dplyr)

xyz <- data_frame(qual = c("A", "A", "C", "C", "B"), qty = 1:5, dates = c("2015-05-01", "2015-05-01", "2014-05-01", "2015-05-01", "2014-05-01"))

the following fails to correctly arrange:

xyz %>% group_by(qual, yr = lubridate::year(dates)) %>% summarise(qty = sum(qty)) %>% arrange(yr)

creating the variable earlier in the pipe chain via mutate likewise fails:

xyz %>% mutate(yr = lubridate::year(dates)) %>% group_by(qual, yr) %>% summarise(qty = sum(qty)) %>% arrange(yr)

note that the class() of the above output is:

[1] "grouped_df" "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame"

if we re-convert the output to a df at the end of the pipe (which I think is equivalent to ungroup()), it works:

xyz %>% mutate(yr = lubridate::year(dates)) %>% group_by(qual, yr) %>% summarise(qty = sum(qty)) %>% as_data_frame() %>% arrange(yr)

Is this a feature or a bug?  Any guidance from this fine community is appreciated.

messages.body_plain:
I imported an excel file with 3 digit zip codes (The ending 2 digits aren't necessary for this task).

The leading zeros aren't pulling into R Studio, therefore, some numbers are 2 digits in R instead of 3.

1) How do I create a new column in R that will change any 2 digit zip code to include the leading zeros?

OR

2) How do I edit the existing column to include the leading zeros?

I've tried this:

DAT$TestOrig3dig = DAT$Orig.3dig.Code
DAT$TestDest3dig = DAT$Dest.3dig.Code
paste("Orig",formatC(DAT$TestOrig3dig,width=3,flag="0"))
paste("Dest",formatC(DAT$Test3Destdig,width=3,flag="0"))

BUT, when I run fix(DAT), those new columns still don't have the leading zeros.

Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Thanks,

Jay

messages.subject: Re: grouping behavior in dplyr
messages.body_plain:
What do you mean by “fails to correctly arrange?” Do you mean that you want the arranging to be on the full data frame, not the groups? If so, then, as you alluded to, use `ungroup` and get that result.

In your “failed” example, you are grouping the data, summarizing within that grouping, and then arranging within that grouping. That is a perfectly reasonable thing to do even if it is not what you are trying to do. To get what you want, you need to group the data, summarize within that grouping, remove the grouping of data (i.e., use `ungroup`), and then arrange the entire data frame.

> xyz %>% group_by(qual, yr = lubridate::year(dates)) %>% summarise(qty = sum(qty)) %>% ungroup() %>% arrange(yr)
Source: local data frame [4 x 3]

   qual    yr   qty
  (chr) (dbl) (int)
1     B  2014     5
2     C  2014     3
3     A  2015     3
4     C  2015     4

messages.subject: Re: Using quantile() with summarize
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

this is an old post, but I'm having exact the same issue, and does;t seem to be fixed. Did you manage to get this done in dplyr instead of plyr?
Thanks
Axel

On Thursday, April 10, 2014 at 10:25:36 AM UTC-4, Content Alain wrote:
> Hi,
>
>
> # A dataframe example
>
> s <- 1:20
> d <- data.frame(S=rep(s, each=100), var=rnorm(n=2000, mean=0, s=1))
>
> # Here is how I would do it with plyr
>
> ddply(d, .(S), summarize, M=mean(var), Med=median(var),  Q=matrix(quantile (var, probs=c(0.25,0.50,0.75)) ,ncol=3) )
>
> # However the equivalent does not seem to work with dplyr, unfortunately
>
> library(dplyr)
>
> d %.% group_by(S) %.%
>   summarise(M=mean(var), Med=median(var), Q= matrix(quantile (var, probs=c(0.25, 0.50, 0.75) ), ncol=3) )
> # Error: expecting a single value
>
> Here is a workaround
> d %.% group_by(S) %.%
>   summarise(M=mean(var), Med=median(var), Q1=quantile (var, probs=0.25), Q2=quantile (var, probs=0.50), Q3=quantile(var, probs=0.75))
>
> Alain
>
>
> On 10 avr. 2014, at 14:28, Stuart Luppescu <pix...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> > Hello, I'm a beginner with dplyr and am having trouble using quantile() with summarize. I am working with a grouped data set. I want to get the nth, 50th and (100-n)th quantile for the variable score.diff for each group.
> >
> > When I use more than one value for the arguments to p= in quantile (e.g., p=c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9)) summarize tells me
> > Error: expecting a single value
> > So, I did three separate summarize calls like this:
> >
> > conf.int <http://conf.int/> <- 0.9
> > intervals <- as.data.frame(summarize(grouped.ts, quantile(score.diff, p=conf.int <http://conf.int/>)))
> > intervals$med <- summarize(grouped.ts, quantile(score.diff, p=0.5))
> > intervals$bot <- summarize(grouped.ts, quantile(score.diff, p=1-conf.int <http://1-conf.int/>))
> >
> > But the structure of the resulting data frame is very peculiar, so in order to reference intervals$med and intervals$bot I have to use intervals$med[,2].
> >
> > Can someone give me some guidance?
> > TIA.
> > --
